{"method":"get_file","path":"CLAUDE.md","content":"# OrcaSlicer AI Redesign — Locked Decisions & Lessons

## ⚠ LESSON: the agent chat is a full, visible conversation — NEVER a one-line input
The user↔agent interaction is messy, multi-turn, back-and-forth, and often NOT cleanly
summarizable. ALWAYS show the ENTIRE chat history as a real scrollable conversation (the
dock), with the settled "Current setup" plan PINNED at the top as the artifact. Do NOT
collapse the conversation into a single input field, a one-line "refine…" box, or a tidy
changelog. The pinned plan is the source of truth for what will slice; the thread below it
is disposable exploration that stays fully visible. (Decided turns 3–4; regressed in turn 6.
Do not repeat.)

## Core conceptual model
- One app = a slicer. Home shows TWO concepts: **Projects** (your work; opens the Prepare
  screen) and **Printers** (your equipment: connection, model, filament/AMS colours,
  calibration, and a **Launch monitor** button). The monitor is a sub-window launched from a
  printer — never a co-equal app.
- Navigation = model **A**: one main window that navigates Home ⇄ Prepare/Check (+ Info) ⇄
  Printer config. Only monitor windows pop out (one per printer, many at once). Opening a
  second project REPLACES the first in the main window; you switch projects via Home. The
  ORCA logo / back control top-left returns to Home; projects auto-save.
- Ownership boundary: the USER supplies what is physically true, what the geometry MEANS, and
  the desired OUTCOME, and holds authority over consequential physical actions. The AGENT owns
  the ~247 invisible process settings (layers, walls, infill, speed, cooling, supports, seams…).
- Printer/filament/colour/model are FACTS ABOUT THE MACHINE → they live in Printer config. The
  project just POINTS at a printer via a loose picker (default: last-used / whatever's idle;
  changeable anytime, never a required first step). Colour INVENTORY = printer; colour→region
  MAPPING = project.
- Painting = annotate MEANING ("smooth face", "bearing surface", "screw hole", "no supports
  here"), and the agent DERIVES the modifiers — not user-set local wall counts / speeds.
- App-level presets/profiles/materials SHIP with the app; most users never touch them. They are
  discoverable only behind the "see all" door, when presets aren't enough. Do not give them
  prime real estate (fold into Preferences).

## Prepare-screen design principles
1. The agent is a SECOND input path, so every visible tool is an OPTIONAL accelerator — anything
   a tool does, you can also just ask for. Beginners talk; makers grab the tool.
2. The conversation is ALWAYS visible (see the lesson above): full history + pinned plan.
3. Four fixed zones, learned once: machine (top) · object on the plate (centre) · intent+plan
   conversation dock (right) · the one commit button, Slice (bottom).
4. Words/outcomes on the surface; numbers/parameters one "see all" layer down.
5. Depth opens as a dismissible layer over/beside the current context; the standing screen never
   permanently accumulates.

## Screen inventory
- **Home** — Projects + Printers.
- **Project window** (one main window, model A) with modes: **Prepare** (plate + tools + dock),
  **Check/Preview** (sliced paths, layer scrub, time/material, risks), **Info** (project
  knowledge: author, licence, safety, BOM, assembly, pictures, versions).
- **Printer config** — sections: Setup · Filament/AMS · Calibration · Maintenance & Privacy.
- **Monitor window** — pop-out per printer: camera, progress, temps, Pause/Resume/Stop, alerts.
- **Dialogs / overlays**: Send (preflight, one-way), the "see all" expert-settings layer,
  Preferences (app-level: cloud, offline, network, updates, presets/materials library).

## Agent setup (decided turn 9–10)
- "Set up the agent" opens a **layer over the dock** (9c) — not a modal, not a chat. One primary
  path (Continue with JusPrin) + a quiet door for the expert paths (own API key · local model via
  JusPrin MCP server). The same sheet is Preferences › Agent. Nothing from setup enters the thread
  or the .3mf.
- Sign-in is a **browser hand-off** (10a–c): Orca waits with Copy link / Enter code hatches; the
  done page always shows the code; on return the layer closes into the first chat with a
  dismissible, unsaved "Connected · who" strip. Connecting creates no card.
- Changing it later (11): the dock's chat ▾ menu carries one last line (dot · path · who) that
  opens the SAME 9c sheet in a connected state (status block + Sign out, plan/quota here only,
  Switch-to door, quiet "Turn the agent off"). Preferences › Agent is that sheet verbatim. When the
  agent breaks, a red unsaved line takes the Connected strip's slot with the fix for that failure;
  plan, thread and Slice are untouched. No agent avatar in the top bar, no gear in the dock header.

## Connect AI tools (decided turn 14) — replaces the "model on this machine" path in 9d
- Direction: Orca IS the MCP server; an AI app the user already runs (Claude Code, Codex, Claude
  Desktop, Cowork local sessions, Cursor, VS Code) connects to the open project. Door in 9c reads
  "Connect an AI tool you already use"; same sheet at Preferences › Connect AI tools. Not a login,
  not a chat, adds no agent to the dock (its proposals wait for approval in the Agent panel).
- User decides two things only: which app · save settings automatically or Copy for manual setup.
  Never types URL/port/key/token/server name. "Detected" = executable or config file found, nothing
  more; undetected apps stay selectable.
- Steps: Choose app → Prepare (generated command/config, Connect… · Copy · Close) → Review (verbatim
  permission question + exact change: command, or file path + old/new entry, others preserved, backup
  made; Cancel is default) → Saving (no Cancel; backend can't interrupt) → "Configuration saved.
  Restart the client to load JusPrin." + backup path. Manual: "Copied. No client settings were
  changed." NEVER say "Connected" — nothing is tested.
- Errors, one at a time, each with its fix: helper missing · client CLI missing · config
  invalid/unwritable · changed since preview → review again · command failed (folded technical
  output) · timeout "settings might have changed; inspect before retrying". Advanced/developer

Of the 13 frames in turn 15 of the Prepare wireframe file, three need replacing and one needs a section removed. The rest keep their layout and need wording changes only. OrcaSlicer already records enough to cover colour changes and switching back to a filament used before, with one gap noted below.

The design server you named is not connected in this session, so I read the project through the built-in design project reader. `support.js` is the canvas runtime and holds no design content.

## Which frames to replace

| Frame | Shows | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 15b | List of remembered spools | Replace |
| 15c | Rename, tune, remove per spool | Replace |
| 15e | New spool with a name field | Replace |
| 15j | AMS slots, remembered spools below | Remove the lower section |
| 15m | Notes; item 5 makes remembered spools the list | Rewrite item 5 |
| 15a, 15d, 15l | Chip, search, after a swap | Keep, reword |
| 15f, 15g, 15h, 15k | Printer menus, Klipper gate list | Keep |
| 15i | Add a printer | Already superseded by turns 18 to 20 |

The design project's `CLAUDE.md` also records turn 15 as decided. Update it, or the design agent will keep drawing spools.

## What OrcaSlicer already records

Your table is accurate for the rows I checked. I found printer agents for Bambu, Moonraker, Qidi and Snapmaker, but none named Creality. Three things are missing from it:

- **Last filament and colour per printer.** Saved in app settings and restored on printer switch (`Tab.cpp:6231`). So "per project" is incomplete.
- **Installed filaments.** The presets switched on for this person, 8 to 13 per printer by default.
- **Custom colours.** The colours the person picked before, saved in app settings.

There is no history of presets used, so the list cannot be in last-used order.

## The design and why

```
FILAMENT ON PRUSA MK4
Colour  ● ○ ○ ○ ○  +
Prusament PLA        ✓
Prusament PETG
Generic PLA
Other filament…      ›
Filament settings…
```

- **Change colour:** two clicks. The swatches are the saved custom colours.
- **Switch to a filament used before:** two clicks. The list is the installed filaments that fit this printer and nozzle.
- **Pick a new filament:** search, then pick. Picking installs it, so next time it is in the short list.
- **Printers that report their trays:** the tray list replaces the installed list.

Every row comes from data OrcaSlicer already keeps, so nothing can drift. The cost is that material and colour become two choices, and personal names are gone.

On the word "spool": use "filament" in the menu, because rows are recipes, not reels. "Spool" still reads fine in sentences about the physical swap.

## Two things to settle

- **Search scope.** In the code I read, search covers installed filaments only. A new preset needs search over all compatible ones.
- **Menu closing.** A real swap often changes both material and colour. I recommend the menu stays open after a click.

content.text:
The chip can follow one rule for every printer: the right half shows the project's filament slots, and a single-filament printer is the one-slot case. I checked the OrcaSlicer code for the facts below but have not run anything. Today the chip shows slot 1 only, per a note in [StatusRow.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp).

A "slot" here is OrcaSlicer's numbered filament entry in a project: one preset and one colour each.

## What the chip shows

```
One slot               [ Prusa MK4 · 0.4 ▾ ][ ● Prusament PLA ▾ ]
Four slots, one used   [ Kitchen X1C · 0.4 ▾ ][ ● ○ ○ ○ Bambu PLA Basic ▾ ]
Four slots, three used [ Kitchen X1C · 0.4 ▾ ][ ● ● ● ○ 3 filaments ▾ ]
Two nozzles            [ Prusa XL · 0.4 / 0.6 ▾ ][ ● ● 2 filaments ▾ ]
```

- **Dots:** one per slot, in slot order, each in its own colour. Slots the current plate uses are full strength. Unused ones are faded.
- **Label:** the filament's short name when the used slots share one preset. Otherwise a count.
- **Hover:** full names and a colour word for each slot.
- **Nozzle:** shown once when all nozzles match, otherwise each size.

## What a click does

- **One slot:** the colour row and filament list open directly. Two clicks to change either.
- **Several slots:** a slot list opens first. Clicking a slot opens the same colour row and filament list. Three clicks.

So the one-printer, one-filament person never sees slots.

## How OrcaSlicer's concepts carry this

| OrcaSlicer fact | What the chip gets |
|---|---|
| Every project has slots, on every printer | One rule, no special cases |
| Slot count is at least the nozzle count | Multi-nozzle printers get their dots for free |
| Each plate knows which slots its objects use | Full versus faded dots |
| Slots and colours are saved per printer | Dots return on restart and printer switch |
| A sync copies the printer's reported trays into the slots | One action fills the chip from the printer |

## What the chip leaves to other places

- **Which tray feeds which slot.** OrcaSlicer matches them in the Send step.
- **Which object uses which slot.** That belongs to the object tools.
- **Mismatch with the printer.** The chip states the project's slots and never warns.

## Decision for you

Should the sync from the printer's trays run automatically or on request? I recommend on request, as the top row of the menu. The sync overwrites the project's slots, so opening a saved four-colour project would recolour it to whatever is loaded.

ORCA · PREPARE · RIGHT PANEL
The chat is the timeline
One authoritative thread per chat, living in the .3mf. Agent turns, hand edits, G-code files and prints are three visual layers in one column. Shown unrolled; in the app it scrolls, header and setup card pinned.
First print
1
CURRENT SETUP See all
Strong · 0.20 mm · 5 walls
35% gyroid · Gray PETG · brim 5 mm
2h 41m·71 g·181 layers
This will hold a backpack. Make it strong, but keep the screw holes accurate.
2
I laid it on its side so the layers run through the hook, and thickened the walls around both screw holes.
Laid flat · 5 walls · 35% gyroid +3
Will it need supports?
3
Only beneath the hook tip. They won't touch the wall-facing surface.
Answered · nothing changed
4
G-CODE a71f 8c04 13:04
2h 36m · 68 g · 181 layers
Sent to Bambu X1C
13:04 · on the printer's SD
Reprint this G-code
5
PRINT FAILED 13:09 → 14:13
Bambu X1C · stopped at 41%, 1h 04m in
Layer shift reported near layer 62. G-code a71f 8c04
Discuss this failure
It shifted off the plate about a third of the way up.
6
That's adhesion, not strength. I added a brim, slowed the first layers and ran the plate hotter.
4 OF 12 SETTINGS
Brimnone → 5 mm First-layer speed40 → 18 mm/s Plate temp60 → 70 °C Layer height0.20 → 0.20 mm See the other 8 →
7
Revert to here
Puts the plate back to this turn and discards the 3 entries below, including the G-code you exported. Files already on disk or the printer stay where they are.
Discard & revert Cancel
8
Rotated bracket to 45°
you, on the plate · 11 steps merged · 15:02
Infill 35% → 45%
you, in Strong · 15:03
9
G-CODE 4f9c b2e1 15:08
2h 34m · 69 g · 181 layers
bracket-v3.gcode
Desktop / Prints · verified just now
bracket-v3.gcode
USB (E:) · modified outside the project
Export again
Ask about this print or request a change…
WHY IT'S BUILT THIS WAY
1
Pinned, always live. It shows the plate as it is right now, never as it was where you're scrolled. Scrolling into the past is reading; the card is the truth you'd slice.
2
Prose, then the diff. The agent says what it did in words; the boxed line under it is what actually changed, in the order that matters. +3 opens the rest — collapsed is the default because the sentence is usually enough.
3
Answers are marked as answers. A turn with no diff box says so explicitly, so the presence of a diff always means the plate moved. No guessing whether talking changed something.
4
Slicing writes nothing. Slice as often as you like; the thread only records the moment a G-code leaves the project — exported to disk or sent to a printer. Full-bleed, hairlines, no bubble and no revert control: this is a file, not a state you can go back to. The hash is its name.
5
Prints are inked. The third layer is a dark band: this happened in the room, not in the file. It names the G-code that ran, so a failure points at a file. Discuss this failure hands the agent the print’s own context. Live progress belongs to the printer, not here.
6
Expanded is old → new. Struck-through before, bold after, four rows of consequence with a door to the other eight. Unchanged-but-checked settings can appear too (layer height held at 0.20) — the agent showing its work, not just its edits.
7
Revert truncates, so it says the price. The control appears on hover on any turn or hand edit; confirming names exactly what’s discarded, G-code entries included. The files themselves are untouched — only the record goes.
8
Hand edits, same timeline, lower voice. No avatar, no bubble, a thin rule instead — but revertable like any turn. Eleven rotations coalesce into their net result; Ctrl-Z still steps through all eleven underneath.
9
Copies, not links. Sending and exporting the same slice group under one hash. Exports to disk are re-verified on view; a mismatch greys out and strikes through and offers Export again. Printer sends state the fact and time only — nothing can be verified there. An old entry’s Reprint this G-code sends that file, not a fresh slice; its place in the thread shows how old it is.

1The Current setup card, at actual size — how much can it really hold?

Everything below is 1:1: a 340px dock, 640px tall, which is what the right-hand zone gets on a laptop. The card’s real constraint isn’t width, it’s that every pixel it takes comes out of the conversation — and the conversation staying fully visible is the one rule this project has held since turn 3. Fixed costs are the header (38px) and the ask box (~54px), so the card and the thread split the remaining ~548px. Heights below are measured from the rendered markup, not estimated.

1aEverything on · the brainstorm, taken literally
First print
240px
CURRENT SETUP · PINNEDundo
Strong — it’ll bear weight
Walls24 Infill15% grid45% gyroid Top layers45 Supportnonebracket arm
~3h 50 · 47 g+36 min, +8 g
Wall at the boss came out 0.79 mm — under your 0.8 nozzle. Widened to 0.8.
2 values edited by you · base preset 0.20 mm Standard
see all 247 ▾
make it strong — it’ll bear weight
Laid it flat, 4 walls, 45% gyroid. Added support under the bracket arm.
how long?
ask, or steer this chat…
Too much. Measured, it eats over a third of the dock and leaves the conversation three visible lines — the thread stops being a thread. And the deltas table is the tell: this is the see all panel leaking upward. Nothing here is wrong, it’s just not all resting-state content.
1bThree lines · one line per job, nothing else
First print
74px
CURRENT SETUP
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~3h 50 · 47 g· 5 changes from preset
make it strong — it’ll bear weight
Laid it flat, 4 walls, 45% gyroid. Added support under the bracket arm.
how long will it take?
~3h 50 · 47 g. About 36 minutes more than the plain preset would have been.
is that support going to leave a mark?
On the underside of the arm, yes — it’s a non-visible face here, so I left it. I can switch to organic supports if you’d rather.
leave it
ask, or steer this chat…
This is the resting state. One line per job: did it hear me (your words, as the title), what will it cost (time and material), how far is this from stock (a count, not a table — and the handle that opens the rest). The card costs 74px — about an eighth of the dock and the conversation keeps seven turns visible. Everything from 1a still exists; it lives one tap down, in 1c.
1cExpanded · the same card, opened over the thread
First print
234px
CURRENT SETUP
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~3h 50 · 47 g· 36 min over preset
Walls24 Infill15% grid45% gyroid Top layers45 Supportnonebracket arm Orientationas loadedlaid flat
on 0.20 mm Standard · undo the last change
see all 247 ▾
make it strong — it’ll bear weight
Laid it flat, 4 walls, 45% gyroid. Added support under the bracket arm.
how long will it take?
~3h 50 · 47 g. About 36 minutes more than the plain preset would have been.
ask, or steer this chat…
Tapping the card’s chevron drops the deltas over the thread — a temporary layer, dismissed by tapping again or by typing. Note what it still doesn’t carry: no risk line (that’s 2f, and only when one exists), no edit attribution unless you’ve edited. Five deltas is about the ceiling before this wants to be see all instead.
2The states, at card width — what makes it grow, and by how much

Same 316px card, every state it has to survive. The rule the heights enforce: only a change you haven’t seen, or a risk, may add a line — and both go away on their own. Everything else swaps content within the three-line frame.

2aJust changed · decays after you’ve seen it
91px
CURRENT SETUP · UPDATEDundo
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~3h 50 · 47 g+36 min
walls 2→4 · infill 15→45% · +support
One extra line, in the accent, naming what just moved — and undo in the kicker where it can only mean “that last change”. Fades to 1b on the next turn or when you scroll the thread.
2bAgent working · holds last known good
71px
CURRENT SETUPworking…
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~3h 50 · 47 g · 5 changes from preset
Greys, doesn’t empty. What’s shown is still exactly what Slice would produce this second — the invariant holds even mid-thought.
2cEstimate recomputing
71px
CURRENT SETUP
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~3h 50 · 47 gre-slicing…6 changes
The old number stays struck through rather than vanishing — you’re usually watching for the difference, and a blank kills the comparison. Background slice, no spinner over the plate.
2dStale · can’t stand behind the number
71px
CURRENT SETUP · OUT OF DATE
Strong — it’ll bear weight
you moved the object — re-slice
Stale is a legitimate state, not an error. It never shows a cost it can’t defend, and it says which of your actions invalidated it.
2eYou edited it by hand
71px
CURRENT SETUP+ 2 yours
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~4h 00 · 47 g· 7 changes from preset
Hand edits through see all land in the same card and are counted separately, so the card stays the truth rather than the agent’s opinion. The agent won’t silently overwrite them; it asks.
2fA risk worth one line
93px
CURRENT SETUP
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~3h 50 · 47 g· 5 changes from preset
Overhang on the arm may sag — show me
One risk, one line, only when real — and it points at the geometry rather than explaining. Anything needing sliced evidence belongs in Check Print, not here. Acknowledge it and the line goes.
2gNo agent configured
36px
0.20 mm Standardsee all ▾
Two of the three jobs don’t exist — nothing was delegated, so there’s no title and no delta. What’s left is a label, and a label isn’t a card. This is the argument for dropping it from the dock entirely in the unconfigured state, as 8c does.
2hSliced, then sent · becomes the record
71px
CURRENT SETUP · SLICED
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~3h 50 · 47 g· measured, not estimated
71px
PRINTED · 2 SEP · FAILED AT 41%
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~3h 50 · 47 gopen this setup ▾
On Send the card freezes and becomes the print-history entry — same object, now a record. Coming back to a failed print means looking at the card that produced it, which is what makes “continue from what printed” concrete.
3Stress test — six ways the content fails, and what the card does about it

The card is four rows, each with its own presence rule: kicker (always) · title (optional) · cost (optional) · risk (optional, max one). Every field’s fallback ladder ends in omit the row — never a placeholder, a zero, or a guess — so anything unexpected makes the card shorter, never broken. Six cases below, worst first. The claim being tested: none of them exceeds the resting card — measured, the worst ties it at 74px and the best is 36px.

3aTitle at its ceiling · 40 characters exactly
74px
CURRENT SETUP
Strong, smooth top, no marks on the face
~3h 50 · 47 g· 9 changes
40 characters is the ceiling because that’s what fits on one line at this width — and because the same string names the chat in the switcher. Past it the line clamps and the full sentence lives in the expansion; it never wraps to two. Worth being honest that this is a constraint on the agent’s prompt, not something the UI can enforce after the fact — the UI can only stop a long one from breaking the layout.
3bNo title · dragged an STL, hit Slice, said nothing
52px
CURRENT SETUP
0.20 mm Standard· ~3h 50 · 47 g
There is no intent to restate, so the row is absent, not empty — and the preset name takes the identity slot inside the cost row rather than a made-up title. This is also the commonest first-run state, which is a reason to make sure it looks deliberate rather than unfinished.
3cNo currency · filament_cost unset, which is the default
74px
CURRENT SETUP
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~3h 50 · 47 g· 5 changes
74px
CURRENT SETUP
Strong — it’ll bear weight
~3h 50 · 47 g · £1.12· 5 changes
Cost in money is filament price × grams, and the price lives in the filament profile — a field most people never fill in. So money is a clause that appears when it can, not a slot: no currency, no £0.00, no “set a price” nag. Grams are always available once sliced, so grams are the promise.
3dNever sliced · the cost row simply isn’t there
74px
CURRENT SETUP
Strong — it’ll bear weight
5 changes from preset · not sliced yet
In OrcaSlicer today the estimate only exists after you slice — there is no background slicing, and auto-slice is still an open request. So before the first Slice there is no honest number, and the card says so in the row it already has rather than growing one. It isn’t a hole: Slice is four inches up and to the left.
3eThree objects, three intents · the case one title can’t hold
74px
CURRENT SETUP
3 objects, different settings
~5h 20 · 96 g· 11 changes
173px
CURRENT SETUP
3 objects, different settings
~5h 20 · 96 g· 11 changes
bracket.stlstrong, bears weight cover.stlsmooth visible face spacer.stl ×4fastest
see all ▾
Three intents can’t be one sentence and shouldn’t be concatenated into one. The title states the count; the per-object intents are the first thing in the expansion, where they replace the deltas list. The resting row stays the same height as every other case, which is the whole point of the contract.
3fEverything missing · no agent, never sliced, stock preset
36px
0.20 mm Standardsee all ▾
Every optional row omitted, and the kicker goes with them — a heading over a single line is furniture. What’s left is a label, and a label doesn’t need a card, a border, or a place at the top of the dock. The degenerate case degrades to almost nothing rather than to an empty frame, which is the test the contract had to pass.

Two things this rests on that aren’t UI decisions. Background slicing doesn’t exist in OrcaSlicer today — without it the cost row is absent until the user slices, and every state above is drawn on that assumption; if it were added, 2c becomes the common case instead of a rare one. And the 40-character title is a contract with the agent, enforced in its prompt; the UI can only keep a long one from breaking the layout, not make it good.

4No agent configured — the card isn’t there, and two things move

The answer is no. Two of the card’s three jobs — proof it heard you, and a durable record of what you settled on — don’t exist when nothing was delegated, and 3f showed what’s left is a 36px label. A label doesn’t need a border, a heading, or the top of the dock. So it’s removed, and the two facts it would have carried go where they already belong: the preset name joins the machine chip in the top bar, and the estimate shows up after Slice, beside the slice result. The rule that governs the other direction: the card is created by the first change to the config — not by connecting, and not by talking.

4aThe dock, unconfigured · no card at all
Prints · 0 Bambu X1C · Gray PLA · 0.20 Standard ▾
↑ the preset name lands here, with the other machine facts
Agent NOT SET UP
No agent connected
An agent turns what you want — “make it strong, it’ll bear weight” — into the 247 settings underneath, and shows you what it changed.
Until then Orca slices from the preset, exactly as it always has.
Set up the agent
Registered JusPrin account, your own key, or a model on this machine.
ask, or steer this chat…
Nothing is pinned, because nothing was agreed. The dock’s whole surface becomes one offer, and the ask box stays visible but inert so the working shape is already familiar. Note what didn’t happen: the 36px label wasn’t left behind as a stub. It was absorbed into the chip above, where the printer and filament already live — the same place a maker with no interest in agents would look for it.
4bHow it arrives · connection doesn’t create it; a change does
1 connected — still no card
New chat
Ready. Slicing from 0.20 mm Standard until you tell me otherwise.
2 a question, answered — still no card
New chat
is the default strong enough for a bracket?
At 15% infill and 2 walls, probably not under load. Want me to change it?
3 the first change — the card appears
New chat
CURRENT SETUP · UPDATEDundo
Strong — it’ll bear weight
not sliced yet· walls 2→4, infill 15→45%
yes, make it strong — it’ll bear weight
4 walls, 45% gyroid. Slice when you’re ready and I’ll have a time for you.
Connecting an agent changes nothing about the print, so it shouldn’t change the screen — a card that appears empty at connection is furniture. Step 2 matters as much: questions don’t create a card either, which is how the card teaches the difference between talking and changing. Once created it stays for the life of the chat, even if you undo back to the preset, because it’s the record of a delegation — and UI that vanishes is worse than a quiet row.
4cWhere the estimate goes · unconfigured, after Slice
Slice ▷ Check Print Print
SLICED · 0.20 MM STANDARD
~3h 10 · 39 g
4 objects · 218 layers
↑ on the plate, bottom-left — where the slice result already lives
The estimate only exists after a slice, so unconfigured it belongs with the slice result — on the plate and in Check Print — not in a dock that has nothing to say. With an agent it appears in both places, and that isn’t duplication: on the plate it’s a fact about the job, and in the card it’s evidence for a delegation, sitting next to the intent that caused it and the delta it cost.

14Connect AI tools — the third door in 9c, redrawn to match how the MCP server really works

9d had the direction backwards: it drew Orca using a model on this machine. What's built is the reverse — Orca is the server, and an AI app you already run (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cowork, Cursor, VS Code) connects to the open project. So the door is renamed Connect an AI tool you already use, and the sheet is a setup flow, not a login and not a chat. The user makes two decisions: which app, and whether Orca saves the settings for them or they copy the instructions. No URL, port, key, token or server name is ever typed. "Detected" only means an executable or config file was found. "Configuration saved" never becomes "Connected": nothing here tests the link or checks that the app loaded JusPrin. Six sheets below, all at the 9c layer's width (~1.5×), one primary button each.

14aChoose app
‹Connect an AI tool
Let an AI app on this computer work with the open project. Orca writes the connection settings; you don't need to know what MCP is.
Claude Codedetected
Codexdetected
Claude Desktopnot found
Cowork local sessionsnot found
Cursordetected
VS Codenot found
"Detected" means Orca found the app or its settings file here. It doesn't mean the app is signed in. You can pick one that wasn't found.
list only. picking a row moves on; no primary button on this step
Six supported apps, detected ones marked. Undetected stay selectable because the person may install it next. Cowork carries its one caveat inline.
14bPrepare setup · a command-line app
‹Claude Code
Orca can run this for you, or you can copy it and run it yourself.
Copyclaude mcp add --transport http jusprin http://127.0.0.1:57231/mcp
Keep Orca open while you use Claude Code; the helper doesn't launch it. Restarting Orca later won't need this again.
Connect…Close
▸Advanced / developer details
generated, read-only, copyable. Copy is the manual route (14e)
collapsed: local address, server start-up error. never an input
The exact command Orca will run, plus any app-specific instructions. Connect… leads to the review; Copy means "I'll do it myself" and changes nothing.
14cReview change · a settings-file app
‹Cursor · review
Allow this AI tool to read the open project and propose changes? Changes still require approval inside JusPrin.
ORCA WILL EDIT
Copy~/.cursor/mcp.json
Copy"mcpServers": { "jusprin": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:52104/mcp" } "jusprin": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:57231/mcp" } … other servers unchanged }
Your other settings stay as they are. The existing file is backed up first.
CancelConnect
the permission question leads, verbatim
previous JusPrin entry struck, replacement in red. long paths wrap, never clip
Cancel is the default; Enter does not connect
For a command-line app this sheet shows the command instead of a file diff. Either way the person sees exactly what will change before it does.
14dSaving → Saved
Cursor
Writing settings…
Can't be stopped once started; it takes a moment.
no Cancel here: the backend can't interrupt a running command
Cursor
Configuration saved. Restart the client to load JusPrin.
Backup: ~/.cursor/mcp.json.bak-2026-09-04
What to expect
· Keep Orca open while Cursor uses it.
· Anything Cursor wants to change in the project shows up in the Agent panel for your approval.
· You won't need to set this up again after a normal Orca restart.
Close
"saved", not "connected". nothing was tested
no disconnect, no test, no auto-restart: not built, so not drawn
Two moments. The progress sheet has no Cancel because the helper can't stop a command mid-run. The done sheet says what happened, where the backup went, and the three things the person needs to know, then gets out of the way.
14eManual setup · after Copy
‹Claude Code
Copied. No client settings were changed.
Paste and run it in a terminal, then restart Claude Code. For a settings-file app, merge the copied block into the file shown and keep your other entries.

````markdown
# Brief: turn 23 — printer and filament chip, without saved spools

## What changed

Turn 15 in `Orca Prepare Wireframes.dc.html` drew a "spool": a saved record of a
filament plus a colour plus a name, remembered per printer. That concept has been
removed from the product. The app now uses only what OrcaSlicer already keeps.
Draw turn 23 at the top of the same file. Keep turn 15 and mark it superseded.

## What OrcaSlicer keeps (design only with these)

- **Filament.** A recipe with a short name such as "Prusament PLA". It is not a
  physical reel. Each one fits specific printers and nozzle sizes.
- **Installed filaments.** The short list switched on for this person. A new
  printer starts with 8 to 13. Order is by brand, then name.
- **Slots.** A project has numbered filament slots. Each slot holds one filament
  and one colour. There is at least one slot per nozzle. A person can add slots.
- **Used slots.** Each plate knows which slots its objects use.
- **Per-printer memory.** The app remembers the last slots and colours for each
  printer. They return on restart and when the person switches printer.
- **Saved colours.** The colours the person picked before.
- **Trays.** Some printers report what is loaded: Bambu with an AMS, Klipper with
  a multi-material unit. Each tray gives material and a colour value. Tagged
  Bambu spools also give a remaining percentage. Bambu has one external holder.
- **Sync.** One action copies the printer's trays into the project's slots. It
  overwrites them. A tray the printer cannot identify becomes the generic
  filament for its material.

There is no history of filaments used, no names for reels, and no pairing of a
filament with a colour. Do not draw any of these.

## Who it is for

Unchanged from turn 15: one printer, no AMS, swaps filament almost every print.
The design must also serve tray printers and multi-nozzle printers without
adding anything to the first person's screen.

## Actions, most frequent first

1. Glance: which printer, which filament, which colour.
2. Change the colour. Two clicks.
3. Switch to an installed filament. Two clicks.
4. Change both in one visit, because a physical swap usually changes both.
5. Pick a filament that is not installed yet.
6. Change nozzle or plate.
7. Use what is loaded on the printer (tray printers only).
8. Open OrcaSlicer's full filament settings.

## Frames to draw

**23a · The chip.** One control, two halves, as in 15a. Left: printer nickname
and nozzle. Right: one colour dot per slot in slot order, then a label.

```
One slot                 [ Prusa MK4 · 0.4 ▾ ][ ● Prusament PLA ▾ ]
Four slots, one used     [ Kitchen X1C · 0.4 ▾ ][ ● ○ ○ ○ Bambu PLA Basic ▾ ]
Four slots, three used   [ Kitchen X1C · 0.4 ▾ ][ ● ● ● ○ 3 filaments ▾ ]
Two nozzles              [ Prusa XL · 0.4 / 0.6 ▾ ][ ● ● 2 filaments ▾ ]
```

- Dots for slots the current plate uses are full strength. Others are faded but
  keep their colour.
- Label is the filament's short name when the used slots share one filament.
  Otherwise it is a count.
- Nozzle is shown once when all nozzles match.
- Draw rest, hover on each half, and keyboard focus. Hover shows full names and
  a colour word for each slot.
- Draw 12 slots. Propose what happens when the dots do not fit. A used slot must
  never be the one that is hidden.

**23b · Filament menu, one slot.** Replaces 15b and 15c.

- Title names the printer: "FILAMENT ON PRUSA MK4 · 0.4".
- Colour row first: current colour marked, saved colours as swatches, "+" last.
- Then the installed filaments that fit this printer and nozzle, current one ✓.
- Then "Other filament…" and "Filament settings…".
- The menu stays open after a click. It closes on click-away or Esc. Draw the
  state after one click, with the ✓ moved and the chip behind it updated.
- "+" opens the operating system's colour picker. The menu closes while the
  picker is open and returns after.
- No names, no per-row actions, no ⋯.
- Draw a 15-row list to test the height.

**23c · Other filament….** Replaces 15d and 15e.

- A search field over every filament that fits this printer and nozzle,
  installed or not. Typing filters.
- Clicking a row selects it and adds it to the installed list. The view returns
  to 23b with that row ✓.
- No colour step, no name field, no "Use" button.
- Two quiet escapes, last: "Generic filament…" and "Import a preset file…".

**23d · Filament menu, several slots.** Replaces the menus in 15j and 15k.

- One row per slot: number, colour dot, filament short name, a mark on slots the
  current plate uses. On multi-nozzle printers, which nozzle the slot feeds.
- Clicking a slot opens 23b for that slot, with a back arrow and the slot named
  in the title.
- When the printer reports trays, the first row is "Use what's loaded on the
  printer…". When it does not, the row is absent.
- Last quiet row: "Add a slot". Removing a slot is not part of this turn.

**23e · Use what's loaded on the printer.** On request only, never automatic.

- A review step, because it overwrites the project's slots. Two columns per
  slot: now in this project, and after.
- An unidentified tray shows the generic filament for its material, labelled as
  a guess. Empty trays are skipped.
- Buttons name the outcome, for example "Use these 4 filaments" and "Keep the
  project's". Keeping is the default.
- Draw the Bambu version: trays plus the external holder, percentage on tagged
  spools only, colour as a swatch with no colour name.
- Draw the Klipper version: read from the printer's gate map, a footer that says
  so, no percentage.
- Draw what the row looks like when the printer is offline.

**23f · After a change.** Replaces 15l.

- The chip and the model on the plate follow at once.
- The material word on the PLAN line follows when the filament changed.
- One grey system line in the thread when the menu closes, one per visit, not
  one per click. Example: "Filament is now Prusament PETG, orange. Heat and
  cooling follow PETG; walls and infill unchanged. Slice again when ready."
- A colour-only change adds no line, because the plan did not change.

**23g · Notes.** What departs from turn 15 and why. Replaces 15m.

## Rules

- The chip states facts and never turns red. Problems belong to the thread.
- Nothing in the chat changes the selection.
- No temperatures, flow values or other numbers in the chip or menus.
- Menus say "filament". "Spool" is allowed only in sentences about the physical
  act, such as "after you swap the spool".
- Matching slots to trays happens in Send. Do not draw it here.
- Which object uses which slot belongs to the object tools. Do not draw it here.

## Carried over from turn 15

- 15f, 15g, 15h, the printer menus: unchanged. Reword "re-picks the spool" to
  "re-picks the filament" in the two notes.
- 15i, add a printer: already superseded by turns 18 to 20. Leave it.

## Housekeeping in the design project

- Mark turn 15's header as superseded by 23, the way turn 13 is marked.
- In the project notes file, mark the spool rules in "Printer + spool chip
  (decided turn 15)" as superseded, and add a section "Printer + filament chip
  (turn 23, PROPOSED, not decided)".
- In `Orca Object Tools Wireframes.dc.html`, frame 22e names the "printer +
  spool chip". Rename only.

## Format

Lo-fi wireframes in the file's existing sketch style. Real content, no
placeholder text. Frame ids 23a to 23g.

## How it will be judged

- Can a first-time user change the colour in two clicks without reading?
- Can they change filament and colour in one visit to the menu?
- Does a one-printer, one-filament person ever see slots, trays or sync?
- Does every row on screen come from something OrcaSlicer already keeps?
````

Two of the five questions expose gaps in my brief, and the sync question has a more complicated answer than the brief assumed. I read the OrcaSlicer code for questions 3 and 5 but did not run it.   pinned card where one applies), attached to the window edge, never a modal. "printers column" = the
  PRINTERS strip on Home (5b). Avoid the coined words "dock" and "cabinet" in labels from now on.
- Six placements for a freeform printer thread (Add + Change), each with a pinned facts card unless the
  UI itself is the artifact: 19a modal chat · 19b printers column becomes the conversation panel · 19c
  main window navigates to Printer config with a conversation panel (config page = the artifact, no
  pinned card) · 19d permanent conversation panel on Home, cards carry state · 19e printer card expands
  into its own thread · 19f = 18b first, correction field grows into a thread on demand. Agent lean:
  19c (+19f's reveal).
- Thread rules (Ken, turn 19 comments): every opening is a NEW session (no carried history); the AGENT
  opens the thread saying what it can do here; chips are specific actions ("Use 0.3 mm layers"), never
  bare Yes/No, and the open input always sits beneath them; a panel header label names where ‹ leads
  ("Printers"), not the current item.
- 19b·Add (Ken): the Add flow in the panel must carry ALL of 18's information in chat form: opener lists
  words / photo / network finds in the FIRST agent message; camera icon in the input row on every screen;
  recognised = 18b card + assumptions line + "Add this printer" primary chip; ambiguous = 18d; network
  = 18c. Photo upload must be discoverable and possible in every thread: a LABELLED "Photo" button LEADS the
  composer (leading-edge attach, as chat apps do, but labelled because it's a primary path), whole panel is
  a drop zone; a photo never auto-sends — removable thumbnail above the composer, optional words, explicit
  send (thumbnail INSIDE the composer box, above the text line); the sent photo shows in the thread as the
  user's message. No dashed drop card (looked like a candidate card, vanished after turn one): the agent's
  opener says how in words. Composer placeholders are a likely ANSWER to the agent's last message; on the first
  turn that is an example answer to the opener ("e.g. bambu a1 mini or not sure, the small one"), never
  "type…". The photo path is a separate, styled TIP paragraph under the opener (red left rule, camera). Primary chips = chip shape, red fill.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` turn 19.

## Add a printer (decided turn 18; 16 and 17 REJECTED — no chat window, no pinned card)
- LESSON: don't convert wizard steps into a chat. The agent's value is (a) recognising the printer
  from ANY evidence — loose words, a dropped photo of the printer/nameplate/box, or what the network
  reports — and (b) knowing what NOT to ask: nozzle/plate/filament get stated defaults, corrected
  later in the Prepare chip (15a) or the project conversation. Setup settles ONE fact.
- Home = 5b. "+ Add printer" → small dialog: "What printer do you have?" free-text field + drop-a-photo
  + FOUND ON YOUR NETWORK rows ("Use this") + small link "Set it up myself" (ConfigWizard, unchanged).
- Recognised → ONE card (profile picture + name) + one line "I'll assume 0.4 mm nozzle, the textured
  PEI plate it ships with, and PLA. If different, tell me here or in your first project" + one
  correction field + Not this one / Add this printer. Correction redraws the card; no thread.
- "Use this" on a network find (Bambu SSDP, Klipper/PrusaLink mDNS) → the SAME 18b screen, card
  filled from what the printer reported (nozzle, plate, AMS slots); sentence says nothing is assumed;
  one optional access-code field; Not this one / Add this printer (Add connects when a code is given).
- Ambiguous words → the agent states what tells the candidates apart, shows 2–3 picture cards, offers
  a photo as the shortcut, and KEEPS the text field (tap, photo or more words all answer); "not in the
  list" → wizard custom-printer page, prefilled.
- After Add: cabinet card on top ("as set up"/connected) + dismissable STARTER MODELS row.
- Manual path (18e) = "Set it up myself" link in 18a or "not in the list" in 18d → the dialog body
  becomes the existing ConfigWizard printer page, unchanged, with a header link "Ask the agent
  instead"; whatever the agent inferred is pre-ticked.
- No agent set up (18f) = 18a's layout with the text field replaced by 8a's connect card (title "No
  agent connected" · one-sentence nudge about THIS screen only · red "Set up the agent" → 9c ·
  sub-line; no disabled input).
  Network finds and "set it up myself" still work without an agent; on return the dialog becomes 18a.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 18; 17 kept dimmed for reference).

## Add a printer (turn 17 — REJECTED, kept for history)
- Home = 5b (projects gallery + printer cabinet). "+ Add printer" opens a MODAL DIALOG over Home with
  ONE question: "Let the agent guide me" (leads) · "Set it up myself". The pick REPLACES the dialog body
  in place: agent → a chat window (header link "Set it up myself instead" · ×; PINNED "New printer"
  card Printer · Nozzle · Plate · Filament shown empty up front, fills as facts settle; thread beneath;
  one input); self → OrcaSlicer's existing ConfigWizard printer dialog UNCHANGED (vendor, model grid
  with pictures + nozzle ticks, Filaments, Bed shape/Firmware for custom; Back/Next/Finish) plus a
  header link "Ask the agent instead". Switching either way carries settled facts; never asked twice.
  No agent set up → agent card greyed "Set up the agent first" (9c), form card leads. Never turn the
  cabinet column into a panel.
- Questions in order, each with its default as the first (bold) tap chip: which printer (words →
  profile match → picture card "This one?"; 2–3 fits → 2–3 cards; "I don't know" → where to look +
  brand chips; not in list → custom profile, bed then firmware, one question at a time, pinned card
  swaps rows) → nozzle ("Most printers ship with 0.4. Did you change it?", only sizes that exist) →
  filament ("Most people start with PLA", brand/colour optional, mapped to a shipped profile else
  Generic) → plate (only if the profile lists >1) → confirm line = pinned card read aloud → Done.
  Settled facts appear as grey ✓ lines in the thread. Connecting is NOT part of setup (printer menu's
  Connect…); the panel says so once.
- Done closes the dialog → cabinet shows the new card on top ("as set up", Connect… link) and a
  dismissable STARTER MODELS row for that printer above the projects; opening one = new project → Prepare.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 17+).

## Object tools baseline (turn 21 — as built, not a proposal)
- 6b redrawn to match the implementation: tool strip is a VERTICAL toolbar FIXED at the right edge of the
  3D view, vertically centred, five buttons (move · rotate · scale · duplicate · ⋯). NO geometry chips
  (cut, mirror, measure…) along the top of the view — they confused people; they live behind ⋯.
- Header as turns 12/15 (‹ Home · two-half chip centred · Slice). No objects rail, no Prepare/Preview/Info
  tabs in the build. Tool uses land in the thread as grey "you · time" lines (raw command names for now).
- Open for next turns: pinned card still shows the preset name, not YOU WANT · PLAN; log lines not yet
  plain words. Wireframes: `Orca Object Tools Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 21+).

## Precise tool values (turn 22 — OPTIONS, undecided)
- Research: PrusaSlicer/Bambu = sidebar manipulation panel (absolute, 3 reference frames, applies on
  field-exit → compounding bug); Cura = 15° snap, Shift free, 90° arrows, no typed angle until 2025;
  Blender = type while dragging (powerful, undiscoverable); SketchUp = Measurements box; Fusion = every
  drag paired with a field. Users mostly want 45/90° one-click; 3-axis Euler entry is an ordering trap.
- Shared contract: drag and type are ONE control · one axis, one DELTA at a time (never absolute XYZ) ·
  snap 15°, Shift free, ⟲90/⟳90 nudges · live preview, Enter commits, Esc reverts, never on field-exit ·
  absolutes behind "see all" · agent is the third door · result logs as words in the thread.
- Placements: 22a HUD card anchored to the toolbar button · 22b value floats on the ring (no card;
  nudges + Lay flat at the view's foot) · 22c tool strip along the view's bottom, swapped per tool ·
  22d pressing the tool posts a card into the conversation (fields + outcome chips; collapses into the
  log line). 22e = the field's four states. Wireframes: `Orca Object Tools Wireframes.dc.html` turn 22.

## Visual system
Modernist design system (flat, Archivo, red #ec3013 on light, 2px rules, 0 radius). The working
files are LO-FI wireframes (Kalam sketch font) — options canvases, newest turn on top, ids like
6a/6b. `Orca Home Wireframes.dc.html` holds turns 1–6; `Orca Agent Wireframes.dc.html` holds 7–11
(dock, unconfigured state, agent setup and after); `Orca Agent Wireframes 2.dc.html` holds 14+. Start a new page when one grows past ~5 turns.
Hi-fi in Modernist comes later.

{"method":"get_file","path":"CLAUDE.md","content":"# OrcaSlicer AI Redesign — Locked Decisions & Lessons

## ⚠ LESSON: the agent chat is a full, visible conversation — NEVER a one-line input
The user↔agent interaction is messy, multi-turn, back-and-forth, and often NOT cleanly
summarizable. ALWAYS show the ENTIRE chat history as a real scrollable conversation (the
dock), with the settled "Current setup" plan PINNED at the top as the artifact. Do NOT
collapse the conversation into a single input field, a one-line "refine…" box, or a tidy
changelog. The pinned plan is the source of truth for what will slice; the thread below it
is disposable exploration that stays fully visible. (Decided turns 3–4; regressed in turn 6.
Do not repeat.)

## Core conceptual model
- One app = a slicer. Home shows TWO concepts: **Projects** (your work; opens the Prepare
  screen) and **Printers** (your equipment: connection, model, filament/AMS colours,
  calibration, and a **Launch monitor** button). The monitor is a sub-window launched from a
  printer — never a co-equal app.
- Navigation = model **A**: one main window that navigates Home ⇄ Prepare/Check (+ Info) ⇄
  Printer config. Only monitor windows pop out (one per printer, many at once). Opening a
  second project REPLACES the first in the main window; you switch projects via Home. The
  ORCA logo / back control top-left returns to Home; projects auto-save.
- Ownership boundary: the USER supplies what is physically true, what the geometry MEANS, and
  the desired OUTCOME, and holds authority over consequential physical actions. The AGENT owns
  the ~247 invisible process settings (layers, walls, infill, speed, cooling, supports, seams…).
- Printer/filament/colour/model are FACTS ABOUT THE MACHINE → they live in Printer config. The
  project just POINTS at a printer via a loose picker (default: last-used / whatever's idle;
  changeable anytime, never a required first step). Colour INVENTORY = printer; colour→region
  MAPPING = project.
- Painting = annotate MEANING ("smooth face", "bearing surface", "screw hole", "no supports
  here"), and the agent DERIVES the modifiers — not user-set local wall counts / speeds.
- App-level presets/profiles/materials SHIP with the app; most users never touch them. They are
  discoverable only behind the "see all" door, when presets aren't enough. Do not give them
  prime real estate (fold into Preferences).

## Prepare-screen design principles
1. The agent is a SECOND input path, so every visible tool is an OPTIONAL accelerator — anything
   a tool does, you can also just ask for. Beginners talk; makers grab the tool.
2. The conversation is ALWAYS visible (see the lesson above): full history + pinned plan.
3. Four fixed zones, learned once: machine (top) · object on the plate (centre) · intent+plan
   conversation dock (right) · the one commit button, Slice (bottom).
4. Words/outcomes on the surface; numbers/parameters one "see all" layer down.
5. Depth opens as a dismissible layer over/beside the current context; the standing screen never
   permanently accumulates.

## Screen inventory
- **Home** — Projects + Printers.
- **Project window** (one main window, model A) with modes: **Prepare** (plate + tools + dock),
  **Check/Preview** (sliced paths, layer scrub, time/material, risks), **Info** (project
  knowledge: author, licence, safety, BOM, assembly, pictures, versions).
- **Printer config** — sections: Setup · Filament/AMS · Calibration · Maintenance & Privacy.
- **Monitor window** — pop-out per printer: camera, progress, temps, Pause/Resume/Stop, alerts.
- **Dialogs / overlays**: Send (preflight, one-way), the "see all" expert-settings layer,
  Preferences (app-level: cloud, offline, network, updates, presets/materials library).

## Agent setup (decided turn 9–10)
- "Set up the agent" opens a **layer over the dock** (9c) — not a modal, not a chat. One primary
  path (Continue with JusPrin) + a quiet door for the expert paths (own API key · local model via
  JusPrin MCP server). The same sheet is Preferences › Agent. Nothing from setup enters the thread
  or the .3mf.
- Sign-in is a **browser hand-off** (10a–c): Orca waits with Copy link / Enter code hatches; the
  done page always shows the code; on return the layer closes into the first chat with a
  dismissible, unsaved "Connected · who" strip. Connecting creates no card.
- Changing it later (11): the dock's chat ▾ menu carries one last line (dot · path · who) that
  opens the SAME 9c sheet in a connected state (status block + Sign out, plan/quota here only,
  Switch-to door, quiet "Turn the agent off"). Preferences › Agent is that sheet verbatim. When the
  agent breaks, a red unsaved line takes the Connected strip's slot with the fix for that failure;
  plan, thread and Slice are untouched. No agent avatar in the top bar, no gear in the dock header.

## Connect AI tools (decided turn 14) — replaces the "model on this machine" path in 9d
- Direction: Orca IS the MCP server; an AI app the user already runs (Claude Code, Codex, Claude
  Desktop, Cowork local sessions, Cursor, VS Code) connects to the open project. Door in 9c reads
  "Connect an AI tool you already use"; same sheet at Preferences › Connect AI tools. Not a login,
  not a chat, adds no agent to the dock (its proposals wait for approval in the Agent panel).
- User decides two things only: which app · save settings automatically or Copy for manual setup.
  Never types URL/port/key/token/server name. "Detected" = executable or config file found, nothing
  more; undetected apps stay selectable.
- Steps: Choose app → Prepare (generated command/config, Connect… · Copy · Close) → Review (verbatim
  permission question + exact change: command, or file path + old/new entry, others preserved, backup
  made; Cancel is default) → Saving (no Cancel; backend can't interrupt) → "Configuration saved.
  Restart the client to load JusPrin." + backup path. Manual: "Copied. No client settings were
  changed." NEVER say "Connected" — nothing is tested.
- Errors, one at a time, each with its fix: helper missing · client CLI missing · config
  invalid/unwritable · changed since preview → review again · command failed (folded technical
  output) · timeout "settings might have changed; inspect before retrying". Advanced/developer
  details collapsed (local address, server start-up error). No disconnect/test/auto-restart (not built).
- Wireframes: `Orca Agent Wireframes 2.dc.html` (turn 14+).

## Prepare header & pinned card (decided turn 12)
- ONE job button, right side of the header, above the dock: Slice ▾ → (Slicing…) → Check print ▾ /
  Print ▾. Slice and Print are mutually exclusive in OrcaSlicer's code (Slice disabled while the
  plate's slice result is valid; Print enabled only then), so they never coexist. Check print shares
  the sliced state with Print: primary when the agent flagged something, otherwise in the ▾ menu.
  Multi-plate: "Print plate 2 ▾", menu has Slice/Print all plates + Export sliced file. Print always
  opens Send preflight.
- Printer chip = printer nickname · nozzle · plate · loaded spools as dots IN SLOT ORDER (never the
  project palette). Capped width, full names on hover. Mismatch = chip turns red and shows only the
  offending fact + inline fix; it's the only red thing in the header.
- Pinned card = YOU WANT (user's words, editable) · PLAN (agent's derived setup) · "Ready to check"
  until a valid slice exists, then time · material. No risk line on the card (dropped as too hard).
- No permanent toolbar: handles + strip (Place on face · Duplicate · Mark ▾ · ⋯) on selection only;
  ⋯ = mirror, cut, split, merge, text, measure, repair. Plate label at the plate's front edge shows
  what's on it and the colours used. Objects rail opens into a tree only when >1 object/plate/colour.
- Header = three zones: ‹ Home (left; no ORCA wordmark) · printer chip CENTRED · job button + ⋯ (right). No
  "Prints · x" chip in the header — print history lives on Home and in ⋯.
- Project name lives in the window title (Mac/Win); Linux shows it after Home. No dirty indicator.
- SUPERSEDED by turn 15 (below) — Printer chip click (turn 13) = popover, ~300px: a list of printers, one card each, EVERY card with
  its own settings ⚙ and monitor ↗ doors (never a shared door at the bottom). Chosen card expanded:
  full names · LOADED one row per slot in slot order ("used" marks the project's slots, ? = unknown
  spool, colour is a swatch only — printer sends hex not a name; remain % only for tagged Bambu
  spools). Others collapsed with status; click body to switch. "+ Add a printer" last. Non-Bambu
  printers have no live data: show configured values labelled "as set up". Read-only; no colour→slot
  mapping here. Red state adds a top block with the
  mismatch + two fixes; one mismatch at a time, worst first (offline > nozzle > plate > filament).
- Wireframes for this: `Orca Prepare Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 12+).

## Printer + filament chip (turn 23, PROPOSED, not decided) — supersedes turn 15's spool rules
- No saved spools. Design only with what OrcaSlicer keeps: installed filaments (brand, then name),
  saved colours, project slots (one filament + one colour each), used slots per plate, per-printer
  memory of last slots/colours, trays (Bambu AMS + external holder, Klipper MMU), one sync action.
- Chip: left = nickname · nozzle (once if all match). Right = one dot per slot in slot order (used full,
  unused faded) + label = short name when used slots share a filament, else a count. >8 slots: unused
  fold into +n; >8 used: dots shrink (ACCEPTED by Ken). Hover = each slot's short name uncut (no "@…"
  suffix) + a swatch per slot + the count.
- DECIDED (Ken): no colour words anywhere (hover, menus, chat line). The app stores a colour as a value
  and holds no name for it, so a colour word would be data the app does not have. Swatches only.
- Filament menu (one slot): [Use what's loaded on the printer… only if trays] · title "FILAMENT ON
  <printer> · <nozzle>" · colour row (saved swatches, + = OS picker) · installed filaments ✓ · Other
  filament… · Filament settings… · Add a slot (one-slot menu and slot list only, not inside a slot's
  own menu). Stays open; click-away/Esc closes. Filament change keeps
  the colour. Other filament… = search, click installs + selects, back to menu.
- Several slots: slot rows (number, dot, name, "on plate", nozzle on multi-nozzle) → slot opens the
  one-slot menu titled "FILAMENT · SLOT n · <printer> · <nozzle>". Same list for every slot.
- Tray row opens OrcaSlicer's own sync dialog unchanged; offline = greyed row with reason; no trays = absent.
- After a change: chip + model follow; PLAN material word follows; one grey thread line per menu visit,
  none for colour-only. "Spool" only in sentences about the physical act.

## Printer + spool chip (decided turn 15) — replaces the turn-12 chip and turn-13 popover
- SUPERSEDED by turn 23: every spool rule below (spool menu, rare actions, Other spool…, AMS slot
  section, after-a-swap line). The two-half chip, the no-red rule and the printer menus still stand.
- ONE chip, TWO halves, parent → child: left = printer nickname · nozzle; right (nested, lighter
  ground, same outline) = colour dot · spool name. No plate on the chip. Slot dots only when the
  printer has slots (AMS / MMU). The chip NEVER turns red — it states facts; mismatches go to the
  thread + pinned card status row (retires 12c's red chip). Hover lifts one half and shows full names.
- Spool menu (right half): title "SPOOLS ON <printer>"; spools the person has used on this printer,
  last-used order, current ✓; click row = swapped, closes (2 clicks). Rare actions (change colour,
  rename, tune with the agent, reset tuning, filament settings, remove) only via ⋯ on hover/right-click.
  Last row "Other spool…" = search every preset that fits printer+nozzle → colour pick → prefilled
  name → "Use this spool" (adds to list). Quiet escapes: Generic preset… · Import a preset file….
- Printer menu (left half), one-printer = 5 lines: name + state (dot + word; ↗ monitor when connected)
  · Nozzle ▸ · Plate ▸ · Printer settings… · Add a printer…. Not connected shows one grey sub-line
  ("Prints go to a card. Connect…"). Multi-printer adds ONE middle section "OTHER PRINTERS" (state,
  ⚙ ↗ per row, click = switch). No fleet UI for one-printer people.
- Add a printer = 3 questions: 1 brand · model · nozzle (everyone's path; network finds listed under it
  as a shortcut — Bambu only via SSDP — picking one prefills the model and asks for the LAN access code
  or sign-in) · 2 plate · 3 "What spool is on it right now?" (same picker). Row clicks advance; Next
  only where several fields exist. Klipper/Moonraker/PrusaLink addresses go in later via the printer
  menu's Connect…. No filament page.
- AMS chip label = what the project prints with (✓ row), never slot 1: one spool → its name; several →
  "N spools", every used slot dot ringed.
- AMS: spool half = chosen spool name + slot dots; menu top section = slots as reported (swatch, plastic,
  % for tagged Bambu only; Unknown → Identify…); remembered spools below. Klipper MMU: same, from the
  gate map, footer says so, no %. After a swap: chip, PLAN material word, one grey system line in the
  thread; the chat never changes the selection.
- Tokens: JusPrin light/dark set (from the brief) applies at hi-fi; wireframes stay lo-fi.

## Add a printer — after testing (turn 20, PROPOSED, not decided)
- Hands-on test of the built app: first-time user didn't know the job or its end, couldn't browse, got a
  confident wrong printer from a nickname, was told a listed printer was unsupported, was told to "tap
  the card" when it couldn't be tapped. 19b stays the placement; turn 20 replaces panel STATES only.
- Identification from the full printer list, answering in THREE shapes the panel draws itself:
  PROPOSE (one card, red "Add this printer" ON the card bottom-right, "Not this one" quiet chip under the
  assumptions sentence, no Add docked at the panel foot) · ASK (2–3 cards each with its own "This one",
  question in one sentence beneath, NO red Add anywhere) · UNSUPPORTED (one agent sentence + a panel-drawn two-row exit block: Browse the full list ·
  Set it up myself; resin printers get one sentence, no exit block).
- Opener = ONE agent message: job + end ("connecting comes later") + question; then the photo tip;
  network rows. No "Browse the full list" chip — the header link is the door. Composer placeholder on one line, ellipsised. "assumed" is
  explained where it first appears (PROPOSE), not in the pinned card.
- Cards: brand on its own small uppercase line, model bold beneath, build volume; rejected/superseded
  cards collapse to one grey line, no button; one live card at a time. Grey activity line "Looking
  through the printer list…" while the agent works, gone when the reply lands.
- Two manual doors, two fixed labels EVERYWHERE: "Browse the full list" (in-panel brands → models, with
  counts, filter, pictures + build volume; picking a model returns to chat as PROPOSE) and "Set it up
  myself" (the ConfigWizard page, 18e, prefilled) — last row of the models list and second row of the
  exit block. Header door of the Add panel = "Browse the full list" (replaces "Set it up myself").
- Photos: staged = 48px thumbnail INSIDE the composer above the text line, ×, file name, "add a note, or
  just send", explicit ↑; sent = the picture itself is the user's message (~120px) with caption, composer
  empty; no readable name → ASK (cards carry build volume) + "I can't read a model name…" + chip "Photo
  of the label" (same picker). Shape-only guesses never PROPOSE. Photo replies say "Looks like…" and never
  quote what a label reads (the model sometimes reports illegible labels).
- After Add (DECIDED design drawn, not the test build): printers column returns, new card on TOP
  highlighted once with "Not connected · Connect…", dismissible strip above the list ("<model> added ·
  nozzle, plate, filament — assumed · Not connected yet · Connect… · Change" → 19b), then the dismissable
  STARTER MODELS row from turn 18. Saved name = model name alone ("Bambu Lab A1 mini", second one "… 2").
  The test build has no Connect… yet; the design keeps it.
- Change panel header door "Set it up myself" = OrcaSlicer's printer settings window for this printer;
  opener lists what can be asked: "nozzle, plate, spools".
- Change confirmation card: title "Change nozzle" · "0.4 mm → 0.6 mm on <printer>" · consequence in
  words · buttons name the OUTCOME ("Set 0.6 mm" / "Keep 0.4 mm"), never Approve/Reject, no tool name.
  After: Nozzle row "0.6 mm · changed" (red), card collapses to grey line, system line "Nozzle set to
  0.6 mm". OPEN: whether a physical fact the user stated needs confirming at all.
- 20h no agent: printers column becomes the panel form of 18f — header ‹ Printers · Browse the full list;
  8a connect card (title "No agent connected", one sentence about THIS screen, red "Set up the agent" →
  9c); FOUND ON YOUR NETWORK rows still live; no disabled composer.
- 20i "Printer settings…" from Prepare on a shipped profile: the change panel, pinned card filled from the
  profile (values labelled "profile"), one line "This printer isn't in your list yet", primary chip "Add it
  to my printers".
- 20j failures, one at a time, one red line in the thread + fix chip, nothing else changes: agent request
  failed → "The agent didn't answer. Nothing was changed." · Try again; network printer offline between
  "Use this" and Add → "It stopped answering. Add it anyway, or check that it's on." · Add it anyway ·
  Check again.
- Orca Arena bundle (OrcaSlicer's Orca Arena X1 Carbon and its Arena filaments) is hidden from the
  add-printer flow — Kenneth, 2026-09-17; still in the wizard. There is no "community profile" concept; an
  earlier label was a guess.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` turn 20.

## Printer conversation placement (turn 19 — EXPLORATION, undecided)
- VOCABULARY (user asked): "conversation panel" = the Prepare-screen agent column (thread + input,
  pinned card where one applies), attached to the window edge, never a modal. "printers column" = the
  PRINTERS strip on Home (5b). Avoid the coined words "dock" and "cabinet" in labels from now on.
- Six placements for a freeform printer thread (Add + Change), each with a pinned facts card unless the
  UI itself is the artifact: 19a modal chat · 19b printers column becomes the conversation panel · 19c
  main window navigates to Printer config with a conversation panel (config page = the artifact, no
  pinned card) · 19d permanent conversation panel on Home, cards carry state · 19e printer card expands
  into its own thread · 19f = 18b first, correction field grows into a thread on demand. Agent lean:
  19c (+19f's reveal).
- Thread rules (Ken, turn 19 comments): every opening is a NEW session (no carried history); the AGENT
  opens the thread saying what it can do here; chips are specific actions ("Use 0.3 mm layers"), never
  bare Yes/No, and the open input always sits beneath them; a panel header label names where ‹ leads
  ("Printers"), not the current item.
- 19b·Add (Ken): the Add flow in the panel must carry ALL of 18's information in chat form: opener lists
  words / photo / network finds in the FIRST agent message; camera icon in the input row on every screen;
  recognised = 18b card + assumptions line + "Add this printer" primary chip; ambiguous = 18d; network
  = 18c. Photo upload must be discoverable and possible in every thread: a LABELLED "Photo" button LEADS the
  composer (leading-edge attach, as chat apps do, but labelled because it's a primary path), whole panel is
  a drop zone; a photo never auto-sends — removable thumbnail above the composer, optional words, explicit
  send (thumbnail INSIDE the composer box, above the text line); the sent photo shows in the thread as the
  user's message. No dashed drop card (looked like a candidate card, vanished after turn one): the agent's
  opener says how in words. Composer placeholders are a likely ANSWER to the agent's last message; on the first
  turn that is an example answer to the opener ("e.g. bambu a1 mini or not sure, the small one"), never
  "type…". The photo path is a separate, styled TIP paragraph under the opener (red left rule, camera). Primary chips = chip shape, red fill.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` turn 19.

## Add a printer (decided turn 18; 16 and 17 REJECTED — no chat window, no pinned card)
- LESSON: don't convert wizard steps into a chat. The agent's value is (a) recognising the printer
  from ANY evidence — loose words, a dropped photo of the printer/nameplate/box, or what the network
  reports — and (b) knowing what NOT to ask: nozzle/plate/filament get stated defaults, corrected
  later in the Prepare chip (15a) or the project conversation. Setup settles ONE fact.
- Home = 5b. "+ Add printer" → small dialog: "What printer do you have?" free-text field + drop-a-photo
  + FOUND ON YOUR NETWORK rows ("Use this") + small link "Set it up myself" (ConfigWizard, unchanged).
- Recognised → ONE card (profile picture + name) + one line "I'll assume 0.4 mm nozzle, the textured
  PEI plate it ships with, and PLA. If different, tell me here or in your first project" + one
  correction field + Not this one / Add this printer. Correction redraws the card; no thread.
- "Use this" on a network find (Bambu SSDP, Klipper/PrusaLink mDNS) → the SAME 18b screen, card
  filled from what the printer reported (nozzle, plate, AMS slots); sentence says nothing is assumed;
  one optional access-code field; Not this one / Add this printer (Add connects when a code is given).
- Ambiguous words → the agent states what tells the candidates apart, shows 2–3 picture cards, offers
  a photo as the shortcut, and KEEPS the text field (tap, photo or more words all answer); "not in the
  list" → wizard custom-printer page, prefilled.
- After Add: cabinet card on top ("as set up"/connected) + dismissable STARTER MODELS row.
- Manual path (18e) = "Set it up myself" link in 18a or "not in the list" in 18d → the dialog body
  becomes the existing ConfigWizard printer page, unchanged, with a header link "Ask the agent
  instead"; whatever the agent inferred is pre-ticked.
- No agent set up (18f) = 18a's layout with the text field replaced by 8a's connect card (title "No
  agent connected" · one-sentence nudge about THIS screen only · red "Set up the agent" → 9c ·
  sub-line; no disabled input).
  Network finds and "set it up myself" still work without an agent; on return the dialog becomes 18a.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 18; 17 kept dimmed for reference).

## Add a printer (turn 17 — REJECTED, kept for history)
- Home = 5b (projects gallery + printer cabinet). "+ Add printer" opens a MODAL DIALOG over Home with
  ONE question: "Let the agent guide me" (leads) · "Set it up myself". The pick REPLACES the dialog body
  in place: agent → a chat window (header link "Set it up myself instead" · ×; PINNED "New printer"
  card Printer · Nozzle · Plate · Filament shown empty up front, fills as facts settle; thread beneath;
  one input); self → OrcaSlicer's existing ConfigWizard printer dialog UNCHANGED (vendor, model grid
  with pictures + nozzle ticks, Filaments, Bed shape/Firmware for custom; Back/Next/Finish) plus a
  header link "Ask the agent instead". Switching either way carries settled facts; never asked twice.
  No agent set up → agent card greyed "Set up the agent first" (9c), form card leads. Never turn the
  cabinet column into a panel.
- Questions in order, each with its default as the first (bold) tap chip: which printer (words →
  profile match → picture card "This one?"; 2–3 fits → 2–3 cards; "I don't know" → where to look +
  brand chips; not in list → custom profile, bed then firmware, one question at a time, pinned card
  swaps rows) → nozzle ("Most printers ship with 0.4. Did you change it?", only sizes that exist) →
  filament ("Most people start with PLA", brand/colour optional, mapped to a shipped profile else
  Generic) → plate (only if the profile lists >1) → confirm line = pinned card read aloud → Done.
  Settled facts appear as grey ✓ lines in the thread. Connecting is NOT part of setup (printer menu's
  Connect…); the panel says so once.
- Done closes the dialog → cabinet shows the new card on top ("as set up", Connect… link) and a
  dismissable STARTER MODELS row for that printer above the projects; opening one = new project → Prepare.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 17+).

## Object tools baseline (turn 21 — as built, not a proposal)
- 6b redrawn to match the implementation: tool strip is a VERTICAL toolbar FIXED at the right edge of the
  3D view, vertically centred, five buttons (move · rotate · scale · duplicate · ⋯). NO geometry chips
  (cut, mirror, measure…) along the top of the view — they confused people; they live behind ⋯.
- Header as turns 12/15 (‹ Home · two-half chip centred · Slice). No objects rail, no Prepare/Preview/Info
  tabs in the build. Tool uses land in the thread as grey "you · time" lines (raw command names for now).
- Open for next turns: pinned card still shows the preset name, not YOU WANT · PLAN; log lines not yet
  plain words. Wireframes: `Orca Object Tools Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 21+).

## Precise tool values (turn 22 — OPTIONS, undecided)
- Research: PrusaSlicer/Bambu = sidebar manipulation panel (absolute, 3 reference frames, applies on
  field-exit → compounding bug); Cura = 15° snap, Shift free, 90° arrows, no typed angle until 2025;
  Blender = type while dragging (powerful, undiscoverable); SketchUp = Measurements box; Fusion = every
  drag paired with a field. Users mostly want 45/90° one-click; 3-axis Euler entry is an ordering trap.
- Shared contract: drag and type are ONE control · one axis, one DELTA at a time (never absolute XYZ) ·
  snap 15°, Shift free, ⟲90/⟳90 nudges · live preview, Enter commits, Esc reverts, never on field-exit ·
  absolutes behind "see all" · agent is the third door · result logs as words in the thread.
- Placements: 22a HUD card anchored to the toolbar button · 22b value floats on the ring (no card;
  nudges + Lay flat at the view's foot) · 22c tool strip along the view's bottom, swapped per tool ·
  22d pressing the tool posts a card into the conversation (fields + outcome chips; collapses into the
  log line). 22e = the field's four states. Wireframes: `Orca Object Tools Wireframes.dc.html` turn 22.

## Visual system
Modernist design system (flat, Archivo, red #ec3013 on light, 2px rules, 0 radius). The working
files are LO-FI wireframes (Kalam sketch font) — options canvases, newest turn on top, ids like
6a/6b. `Orca Home Wireframes.dc.html` holds turns 1–6; `Orca Agent Wireframes.dc.html` holds 7–11
(dock, unconfigured state, agent setup and after); `Orca Agent Wireframes 2.dc.html` holds 14+. Start a new page when one grows past ~5 turns.
Hi-fi in Modernist comes later.
