All four follow-up changes were made in the design project. Below is a summary for another agent, covering the decisions and how to reach the wireframes. I read the design files' markup, not the rendered canvas.

## Follow-up changes, checked

| Change | Made |
|---|---|
| Notes file records "no colour words" as decided by Ken, with the reason | Yes |
| Hover text uses short names with no "@" suffix | Yes |
| "Add a slot" removed from a single slot's own menu | Yes |
| Object tools frame 22e renamed to "printer + filament chip" | Yes |

## Summary for another agent

````markdown
# Printer and filament chip: decisions and where the design lives

## What this is

JusPrin is a 3D printing app built on OrcaSlicer. Its Prepare screen has a
control in the centre of the header that shows the printer and the filament.
An earlier design added a "spool": a saved record of a filament, a colour and
a name, remembered per printer. That concept is removed. The control now uses
only what OrcaSlicer already stores.

## Decisions

Decided by Kenneth:

- No saved spools. No names for reels, no remembered spool list.
- Design for one printer with no automatic material system first. Multi-filament
  printers must work without adding anything to that person's screen.
- The chip states facts and never warns. The chat never changes the selection.
- No colour words anywhere. The app stores a colour as a value and holds no name
  for it. Colour is shown as a swatch only.
- Copying the printer's loaded trays into the project happens on request only.
- That copy keeps OrcaSlicer's own behaviour.

Proposed in the design, not yet confirmed as final:

- One chip, two halves. Left: printer nickname and nozzle. Right: one dot per
  filament slot, then a label. A "slot" is OrcaSlicer's numbered filament entry
  in a project, holding one filament and one colour.
- Dots for slots the current plate uses are full strength. Others are faded.
- The label is the filament's short name when the used slots share one
  filament. Otherwise it is a count, such as "3 filaments".
- One menu holds a colour row and the installed filaments that fit the printer.
  It stays open after a click, so both can change in one visit.
- "Other filament…" searches every filament that fits. Picking one selects it
  and installs it.
- With several slots, a slot list opens first. Each slot opens the same menu.
- "Use what's loaded on the printer…" appears only when the printer reports
  trays. It opens OrcaSlicer's own sync dialog, unchanged.
- More than 8 slots: unused ones fold into "+n". Used slots always keep a dot.

## What OrcaSlicer already stores

- Filament presets, each listing the printers it fits.
- Installed filaments: the short list switched on for this person.
- Project filament slots, with one colour per slot.
- The last slots and colours per printer, restored on a printer switch.
- Saved custom colours.
- Trays reported by the printer, and a sync that copies them into the slots.

It stores no history of filaments used.

## Where the design lives

- Project: "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts" on claude.ai/design.
- Project id: `d981c5e2-20db-445f-9047-fa9e9a12522e`
- Link:
  https://claude.ai/design/p/d981c5e2-20db-445f-9047-fa9e9a12522e?file=Orca+Prepare+Wireframes.dc.html
- File: `Orca Prepare Wireframes.dc.html`. Turn 23 is the first section.
- Frames: 23a chip, 23b to 23b-4 one-slot menu, 23c search, 23d several slots,
  23e sync row, 23f after a change, 23g notes.
- Turn 15 in the same file is the old spool design, marked superseded. Its
  printer menus, frames 15f to 15h, still stand.
- Rules in words: the project's `CLAUDE.md`, section "Printer + filament chip
  (turn 23, PROPOSED, not decided)".

## How to read it from Claude Code

- Use the design project reader with the project id: list the files, then get
  one file by path.
- The wireframe file is about 137 KB, so the result is saved to disk as JSON.
  The page is in its `content` field.
- In the page, turn 23 is `<section class="dv-turn" id="t23">`. Each frame is
  `<div class="dv-opt" id="23a">` and so on. Each frame has a caption in
  `class="dv-cap"`.

## Not yet verified in code

- Whether OrcaSlicer's sync dialog works while JusPrin keeps the sidebar hidden.
- Whether a two-nozzle printer really gets one filament list for every slot.
- JusPrin's nozzle change has no step that re-picks a filament that no longer
  fits.
- The filament search covers installed filaments only. The design needs every
  filament that fits.

## State of the code

On branch `jusprin-newui` at commit `f8b2edb302`, the spool code still exists:
`SpoolStore`, `SpoolMenu`, `PrinterSpoolChip` and `test_spool_store.cpp`. Two
other places read or write saved spools and need a decision when it is removed:

- The Home screen draws its colour dots from saved spools.
- The printer setup chat has a tool that replaces a printer's saved spool list.
````

Replace saved spools with a filament chip built on Orca's own slots

The header chip remembered a "spool" per printer -- a filament preset, a
colour and a name -- and seeded one from the open project whenever a
printer with none was selected. Home then showed that seed as "Loaded" on
printers nobody had described, and the setup chat stored the model's
material word where a preset name belonged. The spool concept is gone
(turn 23 of the Prepare wireframes): the chip and its menu now read and
write only what OrcaSlicer already keeps.

- Chip: printer nickname and nozzle (each size when they differ), then
  one dot per project slot -- faded when the current plate does not print
  with it, unused slots folded into "+n" past eight, dots shrunk when more
  than eight are in use -- and the filament's short name when the used
  slots share one, otherwise a count. The rules live in FilamentChipModel,
  which jusprin_tests covers without wx.
- Filament menu: a colour row (the slot's colour, Orca's saved colours,
  "+" for the system picker), the installed filaments that fit in
  brand-then-name order, Other filament... (Orca's own filament page),
  Filament settings... and Add a slot. It stays open, so a filament and a
  colour change in one visit. With several slots a slot list opens first.
  "Use what's loaded on the printer..." leads only when the printer
  reports trays, greyed with the reason while it is offline, and runs
  Orca's own sync unchanged.
- A filament change follows Orca's colour rule (a preset with a default
  colour brings it; otherwise the slot keeps its colour), through one
  per-slot SetupCommands path the Agent's filament change now shares.
- One grey thread line per menu visit that changed a filament, led by the
  colour it landed on; notes gain an optional swatch for that. A
  colour-only visit adds no line.
- Home's Loaded row shows only trays a connected printer reports.
  printer_change saves the nozzle only, and the setup chat is told what is
  loaded only from the printer itself.
- A nozzle change on the project's printer runs the compatibility pass
  Orca's printer switch runs, so a process or filament made for the old
  nozzle is replaced. That is a real change to the project, and the
  harness now expects the project to be modified exactly when something
  was replaced (it was the opposite rule from 7f66e75b07).

The fake Bambu printer can now send a tray's filament id, as hardware
does: Orca's sync skips a tray without one, so without it the sync could
not be exercised.

Verified on Windows: jusprin_tests 52 cases, agent_bridge_tests 258,
jusprin_fake_bambu_tests 10, AgentUI 204 and HomeUI 61 Vitest tests. Shell
harness: --printer-setup 166 checks and --home-live 70 checks pass (the
tray row opens Orca's sync with the sidebar hidden, and the two fake trays
land in the project's slots); the default run passes 433 of 434, the
exception being print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight, which fails the
same way on this machine without these changes.

Stepping through the spool menu's sub-steps on macOS (Other spool… → Generic
presets → back → pick a filament) and then moving the mouse segfaults the app.
`EXC_BAD_ACCESS` in `PopupWindow::OnMouseEvent2` under AppKit's
`routeMouseMovedEvent`. Seen 2026-09-09 at commit `38c07ba450`.

**Why:** `PopupWindow::hovered` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/PopupWindow.cpp:59`, inside
`#ifdef __WXOSX__`) is a raw pointer to the child under the cursor, and nothing
clears it when that child is destroyed. Upstream never hit this because its popups
are built once. The fork's `HeaderMenu::build()` destroys and re-creates every row
button on each step change, so the next `wxEVT_MOTION` calls
`hovered->ProcessEventLocally(leave)` on freed memory.

**How to apply:**
- Windows is unaffected — the whole block is macOS-only. Do not report it as a
  cross-platform defect.
- The fix belongs on the fork's side if possible (clear/refresh the popup's hover
  target when rows are replaced) rather than editing the upstream widget; see
  `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`.
- When driving these menus with automation, expect the crash after several
  rebuild-then-move cycles; relaunch rather than assuming the click broke something.

Crash reports land in `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/JusPrinShellHarness-*.ips`.

Fix the chip menus crashing, and match the design's chip

Picking anything that closed a chip menu killed the application. HeaderMenu
destroys the popup before it invokes a row's callback, so the menu controller
was freed while a queued callback still held a pointer to it. Choosing a spool,
a plate, a nozzle, or "Use this spool" was a use-after-free every time.

The controllers are shared now, and every row callback holds a reference, so a
controller outlives its popup by exactly as long as the callbacks need. The
popup handle is weak in return, because a transient popup can be dismissed by
the system at any moment and every step has to tolerate finding it gone.

Two more ways the same lifetime confusion showed up:

Rename and Change colour opened modal dialogs owned by the popup. The system
colour panel has no accept or cancel button of its own on macOS, so its window
frame is the only way out -- and the popup rendered above it, covering exactly
that frame. Anyone who opened it was stuck with no way back. Both rows now
close the menu first and reopen the spool list afterwards.

Dismissing a menu left its anchor still painting the pressed fill, because
Dismiss() alone never releases the anchor. close() is public for that reason.

The chip itself now matches the design it was built from: a printer glyph
rather than the abstract mark inherited from the old single chip, solid
disclosure triangles rather than light strokes, and 26 DIP tall rather than 28.
The nozzle reads inline after a middot, as specified, and claims its width
before the label ellipsizes so it can never be overrun by the chevron.

The new-spool and other-spool steps put their title back where the design has
it, above the colour grid and the search field, and "Other spool..." can now
get back to the spool list instead of only being dismissable. The search field
keeps its caret: it is rebuilt on every keystroke, and restoring focus without
the insertion point made typing come out reversed.

Verification, all against the running application: nozzle switch, plate switch,
rename, recolour, remove, import, the two-click swap, and arrow keys between
the chip halves. The harness gained checks for in-place navigation, the chip
resting before its appearance is captured, and the after-swap note as the page
actually renders it -- 288 checks, no failures.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

My review of the code is done, and the Mac build is still compiling at step 218 of 866. Here is what reading the change shows. The Mac run results will follow when the build finishes.

## Verdict so far

The branch does what was decided. The saved-spool code is gone, and the chip and menu read only what OrcaSlicer stores. Four things the coding agent did not highlight need your attention. One is a possible crash on the Mac that I have not reproduced yet.

## Not highlighted by the coding agent

| Finding | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| "Other filament…" opens OrcaSlicer's setup wizard page of checkboxes | Frame 23c drew a search inside the menu. The wizard installs a filament but does not select it, so the person must pick it again afterwards |
| The menu rebuilds all its rows on every click | A Mac-only crash was seen on 2026-09-09 when menu rows were rebuilt under the pointer. I found no fix for it on this branch |
| Dot sizes, gaps and fade strength are typed as numbers in the code | The project rule is to add a design token first, never a typed number |

The branch is not ready to merge yet. The feature works on the Mac and matches the design in its main path, but I reproduced a crash there, and one design departure needs your decision. I built the branch in my own copy and ran it on this Mac.

## Mac results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Unit tests | 52 cases pass |
| Test harness, default run | 431 checks pass, 3 fail |
| Menu appearance | Matches frame 23b: title, colour row, installed list, three quiet rows |
| Crash probe | 1 crash in 7 runs |

The three failing checks:

- **Print preflight.** The coding agent says this fails without the change too. I did not verify that on the Mac.
- **Two colour-click checks.** The fault is in the test, which clicks the wrong position on the Mac. A correctly placed click changes the colour.

## The crash

I added a temporary probe to my copy of the test harness. It sends what the Mac sends: the pointer moves over a row, the row is clicked, the pointer moves again. One run in seven ended in a segmentation fault at the second move. I did not capture a stack.

My reading of the cause: the popup keeps a pointer to the row under the pointer, and the new menu destroys and rebuilds every row on each click. Nothing clears that pointer. The same crash was recorded on 2026-09-09.

## Findings, most serious first

| Finding | Kind |
|---|---|
| Intermittent crash on the Mac after a row click | Must fix |
| "Other filament…" opens OrcaSlicer's setup wizard, not the search in frame 23c | Your decision |
| On a new install the colour row holds only the current colour and "+" | Your decision |
| Colour cells cannot be reached by keyboard | Fix |
| Dot sizes, gaps and fade strength are typed numbers, not design tokens | Fix |
| The colour-click test uses the wrong position on the Mac | Fix the test |
| Opening the colour picker can split one visit into two chat lines | Minor |
| Dot drawn before the slot number | Cosmetic |
| Commit message carries a co-author line | Minor |

On the colour row: OrcaSlicer ships no saved colours, so a first colour change always goes through the system picker.

## Not checked

- The filament list on a printer with two nozzle sizes.
- The sync dialog on the Mac. I ran only the default harness mode.
- Real pointer clicks. The screen tools could not drive this popup in the background.

## Where things are

- My copy of the branch: `.claude/worktrees/review-filament-chip`, with a 13 GB build. I restored it to match the branch.
- The probe, as a patch: `pointer-move-probe.patch` in this session's scratchpad folder.

Here are the four problems written for the coding agent, ready to paste. Line numbers refer to commit `a74862697e` on branch `claude/filament-chip`. I found problems 1, 2 and 4 by reading the code and seeing the menu on the Mac. Problem 3 comes from reading the code only, so the agent should reproduce it first.

````markdown
# Four fixes for the filament chip (branch claude/filament-chip)

All paths are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/` unless stated.
Line numbers are at commit a74862697e.

## 1. Colour cells cannot be reached by keyboard

**What is wrong.** In the filament menu, the colour swatches and the "+" cell
respond to the mouse only. A person using the keyboard can change the filament
but not the colour.

**Where.**
- `FilamentMenu.cpp:64` `ColourCell` binds enter, leave and left-button-up, and
  nothing for keys or focus.
- `HeaderControls.cpp:663` `HeaderMenu::on_key` moves only through `m_items`,
  the row buttons. The colour row is built by `set_header_builder`, so it is
  never in that list.

**Expected.**
- Up from the first filament row moves into the colour row. Down leaves it.
- Left and Right move between cells, including "+".
- Return or Space applies the cell, the same as a click.
- The focused cell shows the 2 DIP focus ring the design system requires.
- After a colour is applied the menu rebuilds. The keyboard position stays on
  the same cell.
- Where a keyboard-opened menu starts does not change.

**How to check.** Add harness checks that send keys through the menu's key
handler: reach a saved colour with arrows, press Return, and confirm the slot's
colour changed and the menu stayed open.

## 2. Sizes typed as numbers instead of design tokens

**What is wrong.** The branch adds sizes as typed numbers. The project rule is
in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, section "Writing UI code", rules 1
and 2: add the token first, extend the guard, then read it from code.

**Where.** New on this branch:

| Value | Location |
|---|---|
| Slot dot size, 8 and 4 | `HeaderControls.cpp:121-122` |
| Gap between slot dots, 3 and 2 | `HeaderControls.cpp:123-124` |
| Gap from the dots to the label, 8 | `HeaderControls.cpp:263` |
````

````markdown
# Fix: the colour-click test clicks the wrong position on macOS

## Summary

Two checks in the shell test harness fail on macOS and pass on Windows. The
app is correct. The test computes the click position wrongly for a control
that sits inside a nested panel. This is a test-only fix.

- Branch: `claude/filament-chip`, commit `a74862697e`
- File: `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`
- Build target: `shell_integration_harness`

## Failing checks

Run the harness with no arguments on macOS. Two checks fail:

| Check | Line |
|---|---|
| `a_colour_click_sets_the_slot_colour` | 3302 |
| `the_line_is_led_by_the_colour` | 3313 |

The second fails only because the first did. The colour never changed, so the
chat line carries the old colour.

A third check, `print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight`, also fails. It is
unrelated. Do not touch it in this fix.

## Background

The filament menu is a popup window. On macOS the popup receives every mouse
event itself and forwards it to the child under the pointer. The code for that
is `PopupWindow::OnMouseEvent2` in `src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/PopupWindow.cpp`.
It finds the child by walking down the window tree and adjusting the position
at each level.

So on macOS the harness posts its click to the popup, at a position measured
from the popup's top-left corner. On Windows it posts to the child directly.

## Cause

`click_row`, at line 2919, computes the macOS position like this:

```cpp
const wxPoint at = row->GetPosition() + wxPoint(row->GetSize().x / 2, row->GetSize().y / 2);
```

`GetPosition()` is measured from the control's own parent. For a menu row the
parent is the popup, so the result is right. A colour cell is different:

- The popup holds a panel, built in `FilamentMenu::build_colour_row`
  (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp:322`).
- The colour cells are children of that panel (`FilamentMenu.cpp:344`).

For a colour cell, `GetPosition()` is measured from the panel, not the popup.
The click lands near the popup's top-left corner and misses the cell.

The call that goes wrong is at line 3298: `click_row(menu, cell);`

## Evidence

I added a temporary probe that computed the position from screen coordinates:

```cpp
child->GetScreenPosition() - popup->GetScreenPosition()
    + wxPoint(child->GetSize().x / 2, child->GetSize().y / 2)
```

With that position, posted to the popup the same way, the slot's colour
changed and the menu stayed open. Two macOS runs, both passed.

## Expected fix

Make `click_row` compute the macOS position relative to the popup for any
descendant, however deeply nested. The screen-coordinate form above does that.

Keep these as they are:

- The Windows and Linux branch of `click_row`.
- The three other callers, at lines 2522, 2942 and 3139. They pass menu rows,
  whose parent is the popup, so the new formula gives them the same position.

## How to verify

1. Before the fix, run the harness on macOS and confirm the two checks fail.
2. After the fix, confirm both pass.
3. Confirm the count of passing checks rises by two and no other check changes.
   My run before the fix: 431 passed, 3 failed.
4. Run on Windows and confirm nothing changes there.

## Build notes for macOS

- A fresh worktree needs the targets `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs` as
  well. Without them the harness has no web pages and tests something else.
- Pass the build directory as an absolute path.
````

One caution for whoever picks this up. The same branch has an intermittent crash on the Mac when the pointer moves after a menu row is clicked. The harness does not send pointer-move events, so this fix will not trigger it, but hand testing the menu might.
